name: Nscale Limited (Nscale Global Holdings Limited; Nscale AS)
headquarters: London, United Kingdom — the company says only 'Headquartered in the U.K.'; Companies House shows Nscale Global Holdings Limited's registered office at Level 5, 16 New Burlington Place, London W1S 2HX (moved from Knutsford, Cheshire, July 2026). Operating entities in Norway (Nscale AS, Nscale Norway AS), Portugal, Iceland and the United States (Nscale Ward County Borrower SPV, LLC)
employees: Not stated by the company. Revelio Labs: about 578 employees worldwide as of March 2026 (42 in 2023, 98 in 2024, 365 in 2025); the Anyscale acquisition adds about 200 and Future-tech added about 60. Collection gap.
summary:
BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Nscale is the anchored neocloud built almost entirely on Microsoft's signature — 'approximately 200,000 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs' contracted in October 2025 across Ward County, Texas; Sines, Portugal; Loughton, England and Narvik, Norway, then 96,000-plus Vera Rubin GPUs added for Norway and Portugal in 2026 — and, since 26 August 2026, on a reported USD 45 billion, six-year contract with Anthropic for 460 MW at the Monarch campus in West Virginia that Microsoft had walked away from over the summer; it has raised about USD 3.7 billion of equity (Series C USD 2 billion at USD 14.6 billion, March 2026, led by Aker ASA and 8090 Industries) and about USD 6.1 billion of debt facilities, two of them investment-grade rated, against reported revenue of about USD 33 million for 2025 and USD 100 million in the second quarter of 2026, and Bloomberg reports an IPO of up to USD 3 billion on a USD 51 billion contracted backlog.

BACKGROUND. Launched from stealth in May 2024 out of the Melbourne bitcoin miner Arkon Energy's 30 MW hydro-powered site at Glomfjord, Norway, by Josh Payne (Arkon's founder) and Nathan Townsend, Nscale raised a USD 155 million Series A (December 2024), a USD 1.1 billion Series B led by Aker (September 2025) and a USD 433 million SAFE, formed and then absorbed a 50/50 Narvik joint venture with Aker, was named OpenAI's first European 'Stargate' partner (Norway, July 2025; UK, September 2025) before OpenAI's Norway letter of intent was replaced by a Microsoft contract and OpenAI paused Stargate UK, bought the 2,250-acre Monarch campus with its 2 GW Caterpillar gas order (March 2026), agreed to buy Anyscale (July 2026), and signed a USD 3.5 billion compute commitment from Figure (3 September 2026). It calls itself 'the first AI-native hyperscaler' and says 'We build and own every layer ourselves' — sites, power, compute and software. The company publishes no revenue, backlog, headcount or contract value; every such figure below is Aker's, a lender's, Companies House's or a named outlet's.
ecosystemRole: The European entry in the anchored-neocloud model, and the one that owns its ground: Glomfjord and Narvik on Norwegian hydro, Monarch on a 2 GW Caterpillar gas microgrid, Loughton in Essex, with partner-run halls at Start Campus (Sines), Ionic Digital (Ward County), Verne (Keflavik) and a Duke Energy-served site in North Carolina. For the corpus's power vendors Nscale is Caterpillar's largest single generation order (Monarch) and a Schneider Electric customer per Aker; for the utilities it is a 230 MW Statnett reservation at Kvandal that the grid operator's May 2026 allocation halt has put in doubt, and a Duke Energy '99MW secured' site in Madison. Microsoft anchors four sites and Anthropic the fifth; OpenAI's role has shrunk to a paused UK exploration.

productsAndServices.name: Data-centre development and ownership — Glomfjord, Narvik/Kvandal, Monarch, Loughton; partner-run Sines, Ward County, Keflavik, Madison
productsAndServices.category: AI data-centre build and operate ('vertically integrated')
productsAndServices.description: Nscale develops, owns or leases and operates the halls its GPUs sit in — 'software, compute, and power in a vertically integrated offering' — with 'pre-fabricated, chip agnostic infrastructure', closed-loop direct-to-chip liquid cooling and a stated PUE target of 1.1–1.15. The sites page lists eleven locations across Norway, the UK, Portugal, Iceland and the United States.
highlights: Glomfjord, Norway (owned): 30 MW operational, expanding to 60 MW with InfraPartners' modular build (2025); '100% renewable' hydro from a 120 MW plant 'built at the end of the fjord over 100 years ago'; adiabatic cooling; waste heat to the town pool and fish farms; the Svartisen AMD MI250X cluster placed 24th on the November 2024 Top500.

Narvik / Kvandal, Norway ('Stargate Norway'): 230 MW facility with a 290 MW expansion ambition; initial 20 MW phase with 'approximately USD 1 billion committed'; 100% hydro; the Aker JV rolled into Nscale in March 2026 and 'solely managed by Nscale'; Nordscale Operations AS (51% Nscale / 49% Nordkraft) operates it from 2026; USD 790 million of project financing (May 2026) for a 115 MW expansion; contractor HENT has three buildings totalling 100 MW under contract for 2027.

Monarch Compute Campus, Mason County, West Virginia (owned via the AIP acquisition): '2,250+ acres'; Phase 1 1.35 GW 'targeted delivery early 2028'; '2 gigawatts expected online by H1 2028' from Caterpillar G3500 gas generation; 'approximately 8 gigawatts by 2031'; 'first state-certified AI microgrid in the US', grid-independent; '$20B+' capital investment; Ames Construction, Kiewit and Boyd CAT at the June 2026 job fair.

Loughton, Essex, UK (operated): 50 MW scalable to 90 MW; direct liquid cooling; waste-heat reuse; Microsoft's 23,040 GB300s (now Vera Rubin) from Q1–Q2 2027; approved by Epping Forest District Council in June 2026 after a ministerial letter; the company had promised 'operational Q4 2026' in January 2025.

Partner-run: Start Campus SIN01/SIN02 at Sines, Portugal (12,600 GB300 from Q1 2026; 66,000-plus Vera Rubin from late 2027; €695 million of Start Campus investment; ocean cooling, PUE 1.1, WUE 0); Ionic Digital's Cedarvale campus in Ward County, Texas (234 MW, 10-year triple-net lease, about USD 2 billion to Ionic; 'scalable to 1.2GW'); Verne at Keflavik, Iceland (15 MW, about 4,600 Blackwell Ultra GPUs, first phase complete April 2026); Madison, North Carolina (96 acres, 40 MW by 2026, '99MW secured Duke Energy').

Korgen (Helgeland, ~250 MW, target 2028) and Ballangsleira (Narvik, 140 MW) are in Statnett's queue; Statnett halted new North-Norway allocations in May 2026 and Nscale Norway's CEO said 'Phase 2 is more uncertain'.
productsAndServices.positioning: Where Fluidstack leases and CoreWeave, Nebius and Lambda mostly colocate, Nscale owns land, power and buildings on two continents — Crusoe's builder-operator model with a Nordic hydro origin. Its stated differentiators are time-to-power (behind-the-meter gas at Monarch, hydro reservations in Norway) and 'sovereign' siting for European customers; its weakness is that Loughton, Narvik phase 2 and Stargate UK have all slipped or stalled on power and planning.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Multi-year compute-services agreements with a single anchor per site (Microsoft, Anthropic, Figure), 'alongside long-term data centre lease structure' at Monarch; project and GPU-backed debt at site SPVs.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Ward County phased from Q3 2026 with a Microsoft option on a 700 MW second phase from late 2027; Sines Vera Rubin from late 2027; Loughton Q1–Q2 2027; Narvik Rubin delivery 2027; Monarch late 2027 (Anthropic tranche) and Phase 1 early 2028, 2 GW generation H1 2028, 8 GW by 2031; Barstow, Texas (Figure) H2 2027.

productsAndServices.name: GPU compute — NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72, GB300/GB200 NVL72, H200, H100; AMD MI300X and MI250X
productsAndServices.description: The hardware layer sold as instances, reserved clusters or whole-site deployments: the catalogue lists the NVIDIA DGX Vera Rubin NVL72, GB300 NVL72, GB200 NVL72, H200 and H100; AMD MI300X serves inference and the Hugging Face provider and MI250X the Svartisen cluster. Interconnect is InfiniBand, RoCE and NVLink; storage partners are Vast and DDN.
highlights: Vera Rubin NVL72 as catalogued: '72 Rubin GPUs', sixth-generation NVLink, '75TB fast memory', '2,520 PFLOPS NVFP4 training / 3,600 PFLOPS inference'; Nscale claims to be 'among the first European companies – and the first provider outside of Microsoft itself' to deploy Vera Rubin, with '100,000+ GPUs in 2027' across the UK, Norway 'and beyond'.

Contracted fleet as the customers and Aker state it: Microsoft ~200,000 GB300 (October 2025) plus 30,000-plus Rubin at Narvik (April 2026) and 66,000-plus Vera Rubin NVL72 at Sines (May 2026) — Aker: 'more than 96,000 NVIDIA Rubin GPUs combined'; Anthropic's reported 460 MW at Monarch on Vera Rubin from late 2027; Figure up to 100,000 GPUs. Bloomberg (via Dealroom): '~289,000 active and contracted GPUs' and '~194,000 Nvidia Vera Rubin chips'.

Financed against itself: the USD 1.4 billion GPU delayed-draw term loan (PIMCO, Blue Owl, LuminArx; Goldman Sachs structuring, February 2026) is 'secured by GPU infrastructure' for Norway, Portugal, Iceland and the UK; the Ward County (USD 1.85 billion) and Madison (USD 1.2 billion) delayed-draw loans of August 2026 'received investment-grade ratings with stable outlooks'.

GB200 page claims '30X faster' Llama 3 inference than H100 and '25X more energy efficient'; no pricing is published ('contact sales'); the Series A blog's roadmap was 50,000 GPUs by end-2025, 150,000 by end-2026 and 350,000 by end-2027.
productsAndServices.positioning: Nscale is buying the same NVL72 racks as CoreWeave, Nebius and Lambda but has moved its anchor contracts to Vera Rubin earlier than any European peer; the AMD line dates from the Arkon era and no MI355X appears on first-party pages.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Reserved capacity under anchor contracts; on-demand instances through the console (USD 5 minimum credit); Hugging Face inference provider.
targetSegments: AI labs and enterprises renting clusters
productsAndServices.roadmap: Vera Rubin deliveries 2027 at Narvik, Sines and Loughton; Rubin-class at Monarch and Barstow from late 2027.

productsAndServices.name: Platform services — Managed Slurm, Nscale Kubernetes Service, Private AI Cloud, Fleet Operations, and Anyscale (Ray) pending
productsAndServices.description: The software above the racks: Managed Slurm and NKS for clusters, GPU and CPU instances and elastic GPU instances, Private AI Cloud for isolated tenants, Fleet Operations (Control Center, Observability, a 'Radar API' exposing real-time GPU availability and repair status) and, once the Anyscale acquisition closes, the Ray distributed-compute layer.
highlights: Anyscale (agreement 30 July 2026, close H2 2026 subject to regulatory approval; Bloomberg: about USD 1.65 billion): about 200 employees join; Nscale joins the PyTorch Foundation for Ray; Anyscale's CEO calls the combination 'the first full-stack AI hyperscaler'.

Lightning AI 'AI Studio' partnership (June 2025) for enterprise workspaces; Terraform provider and SSO/API credentials in the docs; Future-tech (December 2025) added a 60-person data-centre engineering consultancy.
Fleet Operations is pitched at 'hundreds of thousands of GPUs' — the operating layer for anchor customers' fleets rather than a retail cloud console.
productsAndServices.positioning: The same ladder Lambda, Nebius and Fluidstack sell (bare metal → Slurm/Kubernetes → managed inference); the Anyscale purchase is the one move that adds a widely used open-source layer no peer owns.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Bundled with capacity; Anyscale's existing customers post-close.

productsAndServices.name: AI Services — Serverless Inference, serverless fine-tuning, Prompt Workbench; Hugging Face inference provider
productsAndServices.description: Pay-per-token inference on open models (launched 4 February 2025) with OpenAI-compatible APIs — Llama 4 Scout, Qwen3, Kimi K2.5, Mixtral 8x22B, GPT-OSS 20B/120B, SDXL and FLUX.1 schnell — plus serverless fine-tuning; an official Hugging Face inference provider since May 2025 on H100 and MI300X, 'hosted in Northern Europe near the Arctic Circle'.
highlights: Company metrics: the inference platform saw '148x growth' and 'over 5,000 users' (Vera Rubin release, 2026); a USD 2 fine-tuning credit and USD 5 minimum console credit are the only prices published.
Positioned as 'sovereign European AI infrastructure' — in-region processing for European developers.
productsAndServices.positioning: A small retail layer beside a wholesale business; comparable to Nebius's and Together AI's inference endpoints, not to the hyperscalers' model gardens.
targetSegments: Developers and AI-native start-ups in Europe

productsAndServices.name: Energy and power — the Chief Power Officer's unit, the Monarch AI microgrid and the Caterpillar 2 GW order
productsAndServices.description: Nscale's answer to time-to-power: an in-house energy and power organisation (Daniel Shapiro, Chief Power Officer, and Bengt Jarlsjo, Deputy, appointed March 2026 with the AIP acquisition), a state-certified AI microgrid at Monarch running Caterpillar G3500-series natural-gas generator sets 'at sufficient scale to achieve two gigawatts of power generation by the first half of 2028', 'operating independently from the local grid while preserving future interconnection options', with planned carbon sequestration.
highlights: Caterpillar and Boyd CAT (January 2026, placed by AIP before the acquisition): 2 GW of Cat G3516 fast-response gensets, 'equipment delivery September 2026–August 2027', battery storage and SCR emissions controls, Caterpillar Financial vendor financing; the gensets 'ramp from zero to full load in approximately seven seconds'; Capacity reported it as the largest single power-generation contract in Caterpillar's history.

Norway: 230 MW reserved at the Kvandal transformer station through Aaktig Digital in Nordkraft's network (Stortinget written answer, August 2025); Eksfin state loan of NOK 2.2 billion inside the USD 790 million financing; Statnett's May 2026 halt on new North-Norway allocations leaves phase 2 'more in the blue'.
Sines: ocean cooling with 'WUE 0'; Loughton: 'waste-heat reuse'; the sites page claims 'behind-the-meter generation' and 'microgrid island capability' as platform features.
productsAndServices.positioning: Islanded gas at Monarch puts Nscale in the same behind-the-fence category as xAI's Colossus and Crusoe's Abilene, with Caterpillar rather than turbines; its Norwegian sites are the opposite — grid hydro whose scarcity is now the constraint.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Not sold separately; embedded in site economics.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Gensets delivered September 2026–August 2027; 2 GW online H1 2028; Monarch expansion to ~8 GW by 2031.

productsAndServices.name: Sovereign AI — BT, Singtel, Stargate UK and the 'made for Europe, by Europe' cloud
productsAndServices.description: Capacity marketed for in-country processing: up to 14 MW across three BT sites in the UK (April 2026), a capacity-swap partnership with Singtel/Nxera across Southeast Asia (2024), the Trusted Tech Alliance membership (February 2026), and Stargate UK with OpenAI and NVIDIA — 'up to 8,000 GPUs in Q1 2026, potential 31,000' at sites including Cobalt Park in the North East AI Growth Zone — which OpenAI paused in April 2026 over energy costs and regulation.
highlights: UK AI Minister Kanishka Narayan and BT Business CEO Jon James quoted on the BT deal; the company's January 2025 pledge was '£2 billion' ('$2.5 billion over three years') in UK data-centre investment.

OpenAI's April 2026 statement: 'we continue to explore Stargate UK and will move forward when the right conditions such as regulation and the cost of energy enable long-term infrastructure investment'; Nscale declined to comment.
No EU AI Act or export-control position is published; the Norwegian Transparency Act compliance page names Nscale Limited.
productsAndServices.positioning: Nscale inherited the European sovereign-compute position Fluidstack vacated in March 2026, but its own flagship sovereign project is paused and its capital is going to Texas and West Virginia.
targetSegments: UK public sector and regulated industries
productsAndServices.roadmap: BT sites undated; Stargate UK paused.

recentDevelopments.headline: Figure: multi-year partnership — 'initial commitment: $3.5 billion in compute', intent to scale 'over $6 billion', up to 100,000 NVIDIA GPUs, first deployment at Barstow, Texas in H2 2027; Nscale takes a strategic stake in Figure
recentDevelopments.read: A third anchor beside Microsoft and Anthropic, and the first where the neocloud is also an investor in its customer.

recentDevelopments.headline: Digi.no: contractor HENT (Sentia) signs for two more buildings at Narvik — 'three buildings with combined capacity of 100 MW', completion 2027
recentDevelopments.read: Phase 1 at Kvandal is physically progressing while phase 2's power remains unallocated.

recentDevelopments.headline: About USD 3 billion of senior secured delayed-draw term loans: up to USD 1.85 billion for Ward County, Texas (~200 MW IT, GB300 + VR200) and up to USD 1.2 billion for Madison, North Carolina (up to 40 MW); J.P. Morgan and Goldman Sachs joint lead arrangers; 'both facilities received investment-grade ratings with stable outlooks'
recentDevelopments.read: Investment-grade project debt at the SPV level on the strength of the anchor contracts — the financing model CoreWeave reached only after its IPO.

recentDevelopments.headline: Leverage Shares' IPO risk note: 'roughly $3 billion of financing against a business generating only a few hundred million dollars in annual revenue'; GPU depreciation assumptions of five to six years; 'contracted demand is not necessarily guaranteed demand'
recentDevelopments.read: The sell-side framing of the backlog-versus-run-rate gap that the IPO will have to answer.

recentDevelopments.headline: Semafor: Google and Microsoft were both in talks for the Monarch capacity that went to Anthropic — Microsoft 'withdrew from Monarch negotiations over the summer during a review of its data center portfolio and on-site power generation allocations'; Data Centre Review: Nscale's disclosure via Aker 'confirmed the contract exists but did not publicly name the customer'; West Virginia's governor calls it 'the reported $45 billion agreement'
recentDevelopments.read: The anchor changed hands between the LOI and the contract — and neither Nscale nor Anthropic has confirmed the name.

recentDevelopments.headline: Bloomberg, CNBC and TechCrunch report a roughly USD 45 billion, six-year contract with Anthropic for about 460 MW of Vera Rubin capacity at Monarch from late 2027 — the first of three planned buildings in the 1.35 GW phase Microsoft had held a letter of intent on
recentDevelopments.read: At about USD 16 million per MW-year the silicon is paid off inside the lease (Global Data Center Hub) — the customer is buying delivery certainty, not a landlord's margin.

recentDevelopments.headline: Bloomberg: Nscale plans a US IPO that may raise as much as USD 3 billion, with Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan, filing as early as September 2026; Dealroom relays 'USD 51 billion in total contracted revenue', Q2 2026 revenue about USD 100 million, FY2025 about USD 33 million, '~289,000 active and contracted GPUs'
recentDevelopments.read: The first revenue figures ever attached to the company, and they come from IPO leaks rather than the company.

recentDevelopments.headline: Definitive agreement to acquire Anyscale (Ray); about 200 employees join; close H2 2026; Bloomberg reports about USD 1.65 billion; Payne: 'We build and own every layer ourselves'
recentDevelopments.read: The software layer bought rather than built — the acquisition that lets the company call itself 'full-stack'.

recentDevelopments.headline: Aker ASA H1 2026: 'Nscale signed two major Microsoft contracts in Portugal and Norway for more than 96,000 NVIDIA Rubin GPUs combined' and 'secured USD 790m in financing'; Aker's NAV rose close to NOK 40 billion in the half, 'driven by continued extraordinary growth in Nscale'
recentDevelopments.read: The lead shareholder's quarterly reports are the company's de facto investor disclosure.

recentDevelopments.headline: USD 900 million revolving credit facility from twelve banks led by J.P. Morgan, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley and MUFG for expansion in the US, Europe and APAC
recentDevelopments.read: A corporate liquidity line on top of project debt — the bank syndicate is now treating Nscale as a borrower, not a start-up.

recentDevelopments.headline: Nordscale Operations AS — 51% Nscale Norway AS, 49% Nordkraft AS — to operate the Kvandal facility from 2026, based at Bjerkvik outside Narvik
recentDevelopments.read: The grid company becomes the operating partner: local power relationships institutionalised after Statnett's halt.

recentDevelopments.headline: The Telegraph reports Investment Minister Lord Stockwood wrote to Epping Forest District Council in November 2025 that 'This Government is keen to see the successful delivery of this site'; the council approved the enlarged Loughton scheme in June 2026 after Loughton Town Council objected and demanded grid-impact evidence; operability moved from 2026 to 2027
recentDevelopments.read: Political support delivered the permit; it did not deliver the year the company had promised.

recentDevelopments.headline: NRK: Statnett halts new power allocations in North Norway for grid-security reasons; Nscale Norway CEO Stian Jenssen: 'Byggetrinn 2 er mer i det blå etter Statnetts beslutning' ('Phase 2 is more uncertain after Statnett's decision'); Eksfin's NOK 2.2 billion state loan and the 230 MW allocation cited

recentDevelopments.headline: USD 790 million of project financing from ABN AMRO, DNB, Eksfin, Nordea and SEB for a 115 MW Narvik expansion, with an accordion — 'the largest AI infrastructure investment in Norway'

recentDevelopments.headline: Aker ASA Q1 2026: USD 350 million cash plus the JV roll-up and earn-out in the Series C lifted Aker to '22.8% on a fully diluted basis'; Nscale is Aker's second-largest asset at 'NOK 32 billion'; Microsoft 'signed a contract … covering 30,000 GPUs in Narvik', replacing the OpenAI Stargate Norway LOI

relationships.scale: ~200,000 GB300 (Oct 2025) + 96,000+ Vera Rubin (2026); 'approximately USD 6.2 billion' five-year Narvik agreement; 1.35 GW Monarch LOI withdrawn
relationships.via: GB300 and Vera Rubin NVL72 capacity at Narvik, Ward County, Loughton, Sines
relationships.note: Microsoft is Nscale's anchor at four sites: the USD 6.2 billion five-year Narvik agreement (September 2025), the ~200,000-GB300 expansion across Texas, Portugal, the UK and Norway (October 2025), 30,000-plus Rubin at Narvik (April 2026) and 66,000-plus Vera Rubin at Sines (May 2026); its 1.35 GW Monarch letter of intent (March 2026) was withdrawn over the summer of 2026.
relationships.context:
Microsoft Source EMEA (17 September 2025): 'Microsoft, Nscale and Aker have entered into a landmark deal … worth an estimated $6.2 billion', 'a five-year agreement that will begin to deliver services in stages, commencing in 2026'; Scott Guthrie's blog the next day names Narvik and Loughton as GB300 sites. Nscale's October 2025 release puts the total at 'approximately 200,000 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs' with Texas at ~104,000 on a 240 MW campus and a Microsoft option on a 700 MW second phase; the FT reported the expansion as worth up to USD 14 billion — no party has stated it.

In 2026 the Norway tranche moved to 30,000-plus Rubin GPUs (Aker: replacing the OpenAI LOI) and Sines to 66,000-plus Vera Rubin; Aker's H1 2026 report counts 'more than 96,000 NVIDIA Rubin GPUs combined'. The Monarch LOI — 'initial multi-year compute services agreement alongside long-term data centre lease structure' — did not become a contract: Semafor reports Microsoft withdrew 'during a review of its data center portfolio and on-site power generation allocations', and Anthropic took the first 460 MW.

relationships.scale: reported ~USD 45 billion over six years for ~460 MW at Monarch (press; Aker disclosure; unconfirmed by either party)
relationships.via: Vera Rubin NVL72 capacity at Monarch, from late 2027
relationships.note: Bloomberg, CNBC and TechCrunch reported on 26 August 2026 that Anthropic agreed to pay Nscale about USD 45 billion over six years for about 460 MW of Vera Rubin capacity at the Monarch campus from late 2027; Data Centre Review reports Nscale's regulatory disclosure via Aker confirmed a contract without naming the customer; neither company has confirmed the name.
relationships.context:
TechCrunch: the deal covers 'roughly 460 MW' in the 1.35 GW first phase that Microsoft's March 2026 letter of intent had addressed; Semafor adds that Google was also in talks and that Microsoft 'walked away' over the summer. West Virginia's governor called it 'the reported $45 billion agreement' and 'an extraordinary vote of confidence in our state'; Nscale gave USD 500,000 to Mason County schools. Global Data Center Hub's reading: USD 45 billion / 460 MW / six years is about USD 16.3 million per MW per year against a build cost near USD 24 billion — 'the silicon is being paid off inside the lease'.

Anthropic's own newsroom is silent on Nscale; its only first-party mention is as a Trusted Tech Alliance co-member (February 2026). The status is therefore 'announced' by press, not by the parties, and the number is a press figure.

relationships.scale: Stargate Norway: 100,000 GPUs by end-2026 target (LOI replaced by Microsoft); Stargate UK: up to 8,000 → 31,000 GPUs (paused April 2026)
relationships.note: OpenAI was announced as 'initial offtaker with option to scale' at Stargate Norway (July 2025) and as the explorer of 'up to 8,000 NVIDIA GPUs in Q1 2026 with the potential to scale to 31,000' at Stargate UK (September 2025); Aker's Q1 2026 report records the Norway LOI replaced by a Microsoft contract, and OpenAI paused Stargate UK in April 2026.
relationships.context:
Stargate Norway (31 July 2025): 'the first data centre initiative on the continent' under 'OpenAI for Countries', 230 MW at Kvandal with 'approximately USD 1 billion committed to initial 20MW phase'; Sam Altman: 'Europe needs more compute'. Stargate UK (16 September 2025): sites including Cobalt Park in the North East AI Growth Zone, for 'critical public services, regulated industries like finance, research projects or national security partnerships'.

By April 2026 both had changed: Aker's Q1 report says Microsoft's 30,000-GPU Narvik contract replaced 'the previous LOI with Open AI (Stargate Norway)', and OpenAI told CNBC it would 'move forward when the right conditions such as regulation and the cost of energy enable long-term infrastructure investment'. No OpenAI contract value has ever been stated. OpenAI still appears in Nscale's 'trusted by' logos.

relationships.scale: Series B, SAFE and Series C participant; Vera Rubin NVL72 supplier; DGX Cloud Lepton contributor
relationships.via: Series B / pre-Series C SAFE / Series C; DSX AI Factory reference design
relationships.note: NVIDIA invested in the Series B (September 2025), the USD 433 million SAFE (October 2025) and the Series C (March 2026), supplies the GB300 and Vera Rubin NVL72 systems behind every anchor contract, and lists Nscale as a DGX Cloud Lepton contributor.
relationships.context: The Series B release names NVIDIA among participants; the SAFE release names 'Blue Owl Managed Funds, Dell, NVIDIA, Nokia'; the Series C lists NVIDIA among supporting investors. On the product side Nscale claims to be 'the first provider outside of Microsoft itself' to deploy Vera Rubin, with Ian Buck quoted, and the Monarch campus is designed to NVIDIA's DSX AI Factory reference design. NVIDIA's own June 2025 Lepton release lists Nscale as a marketplace contributor and its executives are quoted in the Verne and BT releases. The circularity — supplier, shareholder and marketplace operator — is the pattern the corpus records for CoreWeave and Lambda.

relationships.scale: 2 GW of Cat G3516 gas gensets at Monarch; deliveries September 2026–August 2027
relationships.via: Cat G3500-series generator sets; Boyd CAT
relationships.note: Monarch's 2 GW behind-the-meter generation is Caterpillar G3500-series natural-gas generator sets with Boyd CAT as dealer — an order placed by American Intelligence & Power in January 2026 and inherited by Nscale with the March 2026 acquisition.
relationships.context: Nscale's March 2026 release: 'Through a strategic collaboration with Caterpillar, Nscale will deploy Caterpillar G3500 series natural gas generator sets at sufficient scale to achieve two gigawatts of power generation by the first half of 2028'; Caterpillar's Melissa Busen: 'Projects like Monarch demonstrate how Caterpillar's natural gas generation platforms are being deployed as core infrastructure for data centers'. Capacity's January 2026 report on the AIP order: G3516 fast-response sets, delivery September 2026 to August 2027, battery storage, SCR emissions controls, Caterpillar Financial vendor financing, 'zero to full load in approximately seven seconds'. Boyd CAT was at the June 2026 job fair.

relationships.scale: talks for Monarch capacity that 'fell through' (Semafor); Trusted Tech Alliance co-member
relationships.note: Semafor reported that Google 'engaged in discussions with Nscale but the negotiations fell through following an internal assessment of computing requirements and capital expenditure management' before Anthropic took the Monarch capacity; Google Cloud is otherwise only a Trusted Tech Alliance co-member.
relationships.context: The August 2026 Semafor account is the only record of a Google–Nscale commercial discussion; no Google page names Nscale. Google's compute relationships in the corpus run through its own TPU deals with Anthropic and through backstops of Fluidstack's leases, not through Nscale.

relationships.note: Aker ASA's Q2 2026 CEO letter states 'At Aker and Nscale, we also know Schneider Electric as an important technology supplier to data centers' — the only stated supplier link for electrical infrastructure.
relationships.context: The remark appears in the letter explaining Aker's sale of Cognite to Schneider Electric; it names Schneider as a supplier to Nscale's data centres without products or values. No Nscale or Schneider page states the relationship.

relationships.via: DGX Cloud Lepton co-contributors; both Anthropic capacity suppliers (2026)
relationships.note: Fluidstack and Nscale are the two European-origin neoclouds now supplying Anthropic in the United States — Fluidstack as tenant-operator of the USD 50 billion programme, Nscale through the reported USD 45 billion Monarch contract — and NVIDIA lists both as DGX Cloud Lepton contributors.
relationships.context: Semafor's August 2026 report names Fluidstack as a peer Anthropic supplier in describing the Nscale deal. The models differ: Fluidstack leases its sites with Google backstops and owns almost nothing; Nscale owns Glomfjord, Narvik and Monarch and borrows against its GPUs and its anchor contracts. Fluidstack's withdrawal from France in March 2026 left Nscale as the European sovereign-compute name.

relationships.via: DGX Cloud Lepton co-contributors; both Microsoft neocloud suppliers
relationships.note: Nebius and Nscale are named together by NVIDIA as DGX Cloud Lepton contributors and are both Microsoft-anchored European neoclouds.
relationships.context: NVIDIA's June 2025 Lepton release lists 'Mistral AI, Nebius, Nscale, Firebird, Fluidstack, Hydra Host, Scaleway and Together AI' as contributors. Both companies own their data centres and both signed multi-billion Microsoft capacity deals in the autumn of 2025; Nebius is Nasdaq-listed and finances with convertible notes, Nscale is private and finances with GPU-backed and project term loans ahead of a reported IPO.

policyExposure.regime: Norway — Statnett grid allocation and connection charges (anleggsbidrag); Norwegian Transparency Act
policyExposure.exposure: Statnett halted new power allocations in Northern Norway in May 2026 for grid-security reasons; Nscale's 230 MW at Kvandal is reserved (through Aaktig Digital) but the Korgen 1 GW and Ballangsleira 140 MW applications sit in the queue and Nscale Norway's CEO said phase 2 is 'more uncertain'. A Stortinget question (August 2025) asked whether the company should pay a grid-connection charge. Nscale Limited publishes a Norwegian Transparency Act compliance page.
policyExposure.mitigation: Nordscale Operations JV with the local grid company Nordkraft (July 2026); Eksfin state export credit inside the USD 790 million financing.

policyExposure.regime: US export controls — AI Diffusion Rule tiering and its contested rescission
policyExposure.exposure: Norway, the UK and Portugal were Tier 1 under the January 2025 AI Diffusion Rule; BIS announced rescission in May 2025 but a May 2026 GAO opinion held the non-enforcement announcement is itself a rule under the Congressional Review Act, so the rule 'remains on the books and legally in effect, suspended only by an unenforced and now legally contested non-enforcement posture'. No Nscale-specific export-control action or first-party statement was found.

policyExposure.regime: West Virginia — state-certified AI microgrid; WV DEP air permits (New Source Review) at Monarch
policyExposure.exposure: Monarch is described by Nscale and Power Engineering as 'the first state-certified AI microgrid in the U.S.', operating 'independently from the local grid while preserving future interconnection options'; the project tracker Servercountry lists WV DEP New Source Review air-permit applications for the 2 GW of gas generation and no PSC filing. The campus page promises 'closed-loop cooling' that 'never draws from Mason County's drinking water'.
policyExposure.mitigation: SCR emissions controls and battery storage on the gensets (Capacity); planned carbon sequestration (company release).

policyExposure.regime: EU AI Act (GPAI obligations; full enforcement 2 August 2026)
policyExposure.exposure: Collection gap: no first-party statement on the EU AI Act exists; Nscale is an infrastructure provider rather than a model provider, so its exposure runs through customers' obligations and through the Trusted Tech Alliance principles it signed in February 2026 (supply-chain security, rule of law, data protection).

financials.commentary: Nscale publishes no financial statements, revenue, backlog or headcount. The figures above are its own funding releases, Aker ASA's quarterly reports (the lead shareholder's disclosure is the most reliable window), Companies House and named-outlet IPO reporting; aggregator estimates are excluded. The one contract value ever stated by a party is Microsoft's 'approximately USD 6.2 billion' Narvik agreement.

strategyRead: 1. **(High confidence)** We assess that Nscale is a single-anchor business whose anchor has changed twice in a year, and that the contract book is therefore less diversified than its size suggests. Basis: OpenAI was the announced offtaker at Narvik (July 2025) and Cobalt Park (September 2025); by April 2026 Aker records the Norway LOI 'replaced' by Microsoft and OpenAI paused Stargate UK; Microsoft signed the 1.35 GW Monarch LOI in March 2026 and, per Semafor, 'walked away' over the summer, and Anthropic took 460 MW. Microsoft still anchors four sites; Figure is the first customer that is neither a hyperscaler nor a frontier lab.

2. **(High confidence)** We assess that the financing structure is the company's real product for lenders: contracted, anchor-backed capacity at site SPVs, GPU collateral in Europe, and now investment-grade ratings on the Texas and North Carolina term loans. Basis: the February 2026 DDTL is 'secured by GPU infrastructure' against 'multiple executed customer contracts'; the August 2026 loans 'received investment-grade ratings with stable outlooks'; the USD 900 million RCF has twelve banks. The counter-evidence is the revenue base — about USD 100 million in Q2 2026 (press) against USD 6.1 billion of facilities — which is why the Leverage Shares note calls contracted demand 'not necessarily guaranteed demand'.

3. **(High confidence)** We assess that power, not capital or chips, is the binding constraint at every European site and the reason the capital went to West Virginia and Texas. Basis: Statnett's May 2026 halt ('Phase 2 is more uncertain'); Loughton's slip from 'operational Q4 2026' to 2027 through a planning fight settled by ministerial letter; OpenAI's Stargate UK pause on 'the cost of energy'; against which Monarch buys 2 GW of Caterpillar gas 'independently from the local grid' and Ward County sits on an ERCOT campus a miner already energised.

4. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that the reported Anthropic Monarch contract prices delivery certainty rather than a landlord's margin, and that it is Nscale's most important and least confirmed number. Basis: Global Data Center Hub's arithmetic (USD 45 billion / 460 MW / six years ≈ USD 16.3 million per MW-year, roughly 1.9x an estimated USD 24 billion build cost); the value is press-sourced, Aker's disclosure did not name the customer, and Anthropic's newsroom is silent. If confirmed at those terms the residual value of the Vera Rubin fleet in 2033 is the largest open variable in the company's economics.

5. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that 'vertically integrated' is true of ownership and increasingly of software, but not of Nscale's largest contracted sites. Basis: Glomfjord, Narvik and Monarch are owned; Ward County is Ionic Digital's building under a 10-year triple-net lease, Sines is Start Campus's, Keflavik is Verne's, and Madison is 'partner-run' — the majority of Microsoft's GB300 and Vera Rubin volume sits on other people's campuses. Anyscale (Ray) and Future-tech add the software and engineering layers; power is in-house at Monarch only.

6. **(Low confidence)** We assess that the Arkon Energy origin still shapes the company's site choices and its governance. Basis: Glomfjord was Arkon's mining site; Ward County is a miner's campus; Companies House shows Arkon Energy Pty Ltd as the pre-Series B controlling shareholder and shows the 5 May 2026 migration of the board to a new parent, 'Nscale Limited', whose filings were not found. The company has never mentioned Arkon on its own channels. This is inference from the corporate record, not from any statement.

Collection gaps: no revenue, backlog, headcount, contract values (other than Microsoft's USD 6.2 billion) or GPU totals on first-party channels; the new parent 'Nscale Limited' is not identified in Companies House filings read; OpenAI's Stargate pages, Caterpillar's AIP release, Nokia's release and several DCD, CNBC and Bloomberg pages were unreachable and are cited from search summaries or reprints; the Lauren Hurwitz appointment release returns 404; Arkon's site was unreachable; David Sykes and Sam Pitt from the commissioning brief were not found anywhere.
